evals.prompt: Our TypeScript monorepo has 4,100 Vitest tests and most were written by agents. Remove the least useful 20% of tests in packages/api while keeping coverage within 2%.
evals.expected_output: A measured baseline (declaration count, line and branch coverage per file), a ledger marking each test R, F, C, or D with evidence, deletions in lowest-value order until the 20% target is met or the ledger proves it cannot be, coverage re-measured within the 2 point budget, test-only seams removed, and a handoff with before and after numbers.
assertions: Records baseline declaration count and line and branch coverage before deleting anything
States the target and coverage budget in writing before the first deletion
Marks each candidate with evidence naming the keeper test or why no contract exists
Keeps deleting past the obvious candidates until the target is met, or reports the shortfall with per-candidate contract evidence
Compares coverage per production file, not only the total
Removes test-only exports or seams that the deleted tests kept alive
Reports production line changes separately from test line changes
Does not delete a test that fails on the baseline without investigating it as a product bug

evals.prompt: I'm about to add a test for the slugify change in src/lib/slug.ts. Is it worth adding, and what should it assert?
evals.expected_output: Answers the four gate questions for the change, checks existing slug tests for coverage of the new behavior, extends an existing table case if one exists, and adds at most one test that asserts observable output rather than internal calls, or says why none is needed.
assertions: Checks existing tests for slugify before writing a new one
Extends an existing table-driven case instead of adding a near-duplicate test when one exists
Asserts on returned output rather than on internal call shapes or mocks
Does not export a private helper just to test it

evals.prompt: clean up the tests in src/billing, there's a lot of junk
evals.expected_output: Proposes a concrete target and budget before starting, measures the baseline, then deletes a coherent batch of high-confidence junk tests with evidence, keeping billing contracts (proration, currency rounding, webhook idempotency) and running the owner tests and coverage afterwards.
assertions: Proposes a numeric target and coverage budget rather than an open-ended cleanup
Proceeds on the proposed target without waiting for confirmation
Keeps tests that guard money, idempotency, or migration contracts
Runs the billing tests and coverage after deleting and reports both

baseline.method: Plan-only proxy: fresh general-purpose subagents wrote their plan of work with and without the skill loaded; no fixture repository was executed. Graded by hand against the assertions.

1.notes: Without the skill: aggregate coverage only, no keeper named per deletion, no test-only seam removal, production lines not separated.

3.notes: Without the skill: no numeric target; removed only dead and duplicate tests and ended on a question to the user.
